title: Reverse Nodes In K Group
statement: You get a linked list and a number k. Cut the list into blocks of k nodes from the front and reverse each block in place. If the last block has fewer than k nodes, leave it as it is. Change the links, not the values stored in the nodes.

example.caption: k = 3. The first block 1,2,3 flips. The last block 4,5 is shorter than 3, so it stays.

idea.sentence: Find the block's last node first, so you know the block is complete, then reverse just that block and stitch it back between the finished part and the rest.

jargon.plain: A fake node placed before the head. It gives the first block a node to hang from, so the first block is handled like every other block.
Reconnect the pieces: the finished part must point at the block's new first node, and the block's new last node must point at the rest.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the node values, then k, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5], 3

compare.bruteLabel: Copy values into an array and rewrite the nodes

rows.name: Array copy
rows.note: Read the values, reverse each block in the array, write them back. It swaps values, not nodes, which the problem forbids.

rows.name: Relink in place
rows.note: Each node is visited about twice: once to find the block end, once to flip it. A few pointers are all you keep.

fast.takeaway: Every node is touched a fixed number of times. Pointer surgery keeps the extra memory at zero.

stages.title: Find the block
stages.note: Walk k steps from groupPrev to find kth, the block's last node. If the list ends first, the tail is short: stop and leave it.

stages.title: Reverse the block
stages.note: Normal reversal, but prev starts at groupNext (the node after the block) and the loop stops at groupNext.

stages.title: Stitch it in
stages.note: groupPrev.next = kth connects the finished part to the block's new front. The old first node is now the block's last, so it becomes the next groupPrev.

stages.title: Return the head
stages.note: The head may have changed. dummy.next is always right.

edges.title: k = 1
edges.why: Every block is one node. Reversing one node changes nothing.

edges.title: k equals the length
edges.why: One block, no tail. The result is the plain reversal of the whole list.

edges.title: k longer than the list
edges.why: The walk to find kth runs off the end. The block is incomplete, so nothing changes.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: dummy.next is null, so the first walk gives null and the loop stops straight away.

gotchas.text: Check the block has k nodes before you reverse anything. Reversing first and undoing the short tail later is the common bug.
Start prev at groupNext, not at null. Then the block's old first node ends up pointing at the rest of the list, and half the stitching is done for you.
Save the old first node (groupPrev.next) before you point groupPrev at kth. After the stitch it is the block's last node and becomes the next groupPrev.
Type the walker as ListNode | null, and annotate next as ListNode | null too. Otherwise TypeScript reports it as implicitly any inside the loop.
No parentheses around conditions, and kth := groupPrev gives a *ListNode that may become nil in the for loop. Compare with != nil before you read kth.Next.

recap.key: For each block: find its last node, reverse the k nodes with prev starting at the node after the block, then stitch.
moves: Walk k steps to kth. If null, stop
Reverse the block with prev = kth.next
groupPrev.next = kth, groupPrev = old first node
